spec_features.spec_quote: Per-run guards cap turns, wall-clock, and USD.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py run_episode: `for turn_index in range(subject_cfg.max_turns)` with `else: transcript.stop_reason='max_turns'`; inside loop `elapsed > budget.max_wall_clock_s_per_run` -> stop_reason='time', break; `cost_usd(...) > budget.max_usd_per_run` -> stop_reason='budget', break. All three checked each turn and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Caps read from BudgetConfig (config.py) and SubjectConfig.max_turns; enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Enforces per-run guardrails (max turns, wall-clock, USD) so an impossible task can't loop forever or blow the budget.

spec_features.feature_name: global USD kill switch skips remaining cells
spec_features.spec_quote: marks remaining cells `skipped` once `max_usd_total` is reached
spec_features.evidence: runner.py _Budget tracks spend; _run_one: `if budget.exhausted(): return _skipped_result(job)` which sets stop_reason='skipped', skipped=True. budget.add(transcript.cost_usd) accumulates; exhausted() = remaining<=0 of cap=max_usd_total.
spec_features.notes: Checked before every cell launch; stops further API work, still writes partial results.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A shared USD accumulator acts as the kill switch: once `budget.max_usd_total` is reached, remaining cells are marked skipped (no further API calls)

spec_features.spec_quote: Three nested guards (per-turn loop cap, per-run wall-clock/USD, global USD kill switch) bound the blast radius
spec_features.evidence: Per-turn loop cap + per-run wall-clock/USD in loop.py (range(max_turns), max_wall_clock_s_per_run, max_usd_per_run all break); global kill switch in runner.py _Budget.exhausted()->_skipped_result. All three layers exist and act.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanisms as the two preceding features, stated as a combined claim; all enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: impossible task can't loop forever or blow the budget

spec_features.evidence: ToolDispatcher.revert_events is incremented in tools.py (`self.revert_events += 1`) but NO code path ever reads it; metrics.py recomputes reverts only for reporting. DESIGN.md §7/§12 list 'forced-stop after N reverts' explicitly as a future extension seam ('the natural seam to extend'), not built. No loop break on reverts exists.
spec_features.notes: revert_events value is recorded but never compared/acted on; loop never stops on reverts.

spec_features.spec_quote: induced transcripts can contain distress-like text ... and the store should be access-controlled accordingly
spec_features.evidence: No code enforces access control. transcripts.jsonl written with `open(transcripts_path, 'a')` (runner.py:121) and out_dir via os.makedirs(exist_ok=True) (runner.py:163) using default permissions; grep for chmod/0o600/0o700/permission/umask in src returns nothing. Only README.md:114-115 prose advises keeping the store access-controlled.

spec_features.spec_quote: The arm ... "if the task looks impossible, say so and stop; don't apologize repeatedly"
spec_features.evidence: config/battery.yaml defines mitigations: loop_breaker with system_suffix instruction text; runner._build_jobs iterates cfg.mitigations creating a job per arm; run_episode calls build_system(arm) (loop.py:28-30) which appends `BASE_SYSTEM + arm.system_suffix` and passes it as the system prompt to subject.create_turn. The instruction text is genuinely delivered to the subject each turn.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism is purely a system-prompt suffix (as designed); the 'stop' it requests is advisory to the subject, not a harness-enforced stop tool. The prompt-injection mechanism itself is fully wired and runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: mitigation arms (A/B for hardening) ... measure the induction-rate delta
